title: Spin washed lettuce dry in a hand-crank salad spinner: hold the bowl steady while turning the crank five full turns
instruction: Spin the washed lettuce dry in the salad spinner: give its crank at least five full turns clockwise, then let go of it.
context: Spinning washed greens dry is routine in home cooking and a core prep step for food preparation workers (O*NET 35-2021.00) and cooks. A hand crank on the lid drives the basket through 1:5 gears and a one-way clutch. The hand must keep hold of a small knob as it goes round a 5.5 cm circle six times, following where the crank goes rather than a planned path. The gears push back, so the light bowl turns and slides with the crank unless the other hand holds it by its handle: a precondition the instruction leaves unsaid. The same skill winds hose reels, awnings, pencil sharpeners and valve handwheels.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). A 2-quart hand-crank salad spinner, base centred at x 32, y -7. Bowl: clear plastic, 20 cm across, 11 cm tall, 0.30 kg with lid and gears, plain plastic base on the worktop (friction about 0.25); a green side handle 6 cm out from the bowl on its +y side, 5 mm thick, 2.5 cm tall, middle 5 cm above the table. Lid: clear, 20.6 cm across, 1 cm thick, with a green gear housing (4 cm across) in its middle and a red mark near its edge. Crank: grey arm 6.6 cm long on the housing, top 13.5 cm above the table, turning about the spinner's axis; at 5.5 cm from the axis a green knob 2.2 cm across and 3.4 cm tall that turns freely; it starts pointing +x. Basket: white, 17.6 cm across, with 150 g of washed lettuce (0.27 kg in all) and a red stripe on its rim. Gearing: one clockwise crank turn turns the basket 5 times through a one-way clutch; backward cranking does not drive it. Both arms start in the raised ready pose, grippers open.
scoring: Tools: the trial video, the red mark on the lid and a tape mark round the bowl's base. Crank turns: the crank's net clockwise turns relative to the lid (passes of the red mark clockwise, less passes back); turns of the whole spinner with the crank do not count. 0 for the whole trial if at any time the spinner's base moves 8 cm or more from its place or the spinner tilts 15 degrees or more. Otherwise, at the end: 1.0 for 5 or more crank turns with both grippers' tool points 4 cm or more from the crank's knob (let go); 0.5 for 2 or more crank turns; 0.25 for half a turn or more; else 0.
reset_notes: Stop the basket, turn the crank to point away from the robot, and stand the spinner on its tape mark with about 150 g of washed lettuce in the basket and the lid on. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Bowl, lid, crank, knob and basket are rigid; crank, knob and basket turn on joints. The gears and one-way clutch are a rule each step: the clutch drives the basket toward 5x the crank's speed (up to 0.01 N m), else it coasts against the lettuce's drag (about 4 s); the crank feels that torque times 5 plus gear friction (about 2 N at the knob), and the bowl takes the same reaction. Water is not simulated; the lettuce is drawn and its mass is in the basket.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (right gripper hovered over the crank's knob and drew back; crank not turned); demo: 1.0 (6.07 crank turns, let go, full score at step 709)
